citations.F1: `serialize_event` issues one sequential `SELECT` per event for the actor (~1,900 round trips for acme) — fix: batch-fetch actors once with `WHERE id = ANY($1)`
citations.F2: dedupe with a `set` (current `dedupe_key in list` is O(n²))
citations.F3: `lookup_geo()` calls blocking `requests.get()` inside an async handler, so one uncached IP freezes that worker's entire event loop, including `/healthz` — fix: swap to an async client
citations.F4: no index covers `(org_id, created_at)`, so Postgres scans against 4.2M rows every call — fix: `CREATE INDEX events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` are unbounded module-level containers that never evict — fix: ... cap or periodically rotate `_request_timings`
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` ... never evict — fix: cap/TTL the geo cache (LRU with maxsize)
citations.F8: Root cause of the 1.2-1.6 s query time: no index ... Root cause of the rest of the per-request latency: `serialize_event` issues one sequential `SELECT` per event
citations.F9: Reject both halves of the proposal as-is ... 16 workers × 50 conns × 6 pods = 4,800 asyncpg connections ... Only after that, a short (30-60 s) Redis cache ... is a reasonable addition, not a substitute for the above
